- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I've now read every touched file and the supporting `showModal`/render code. Let me complete my analysis.

**Phase 1 — Entry points and sinks introduced by this change:**
- New global `window.selectDream(dreamId)` callable from an inline `onclick`
- Daily pipeline step `checkDreamProgress` 
- DOM sinks: `dreamEl.innerHTML` in `renderDreamSection`; inline `onclick="selectDream('...')"` template-built in `showDreamSelectModal`; `box.innerHTML` via `showModal({body})` in both new modals
- `StateManager.addMessage(...)` invoked from `checkDreamProgress` and `selectDream`

**Phase 2 — Data flow tracing:**

Every value flowing into the new innerHTML/template sinks is derived from the **statically-defined `DREAMS` array** literal in `dreams.js`:
- `dream.icon`, `dream.name`, `dream.desc`, `milestone.title`, `milestone.story`, `d.id` — all hard-coded strings in the source
- `progress` — `Math.round` of integer arithmetic → numeric
- `curTitle` — comes from `dream.milestones[idx].title` (static)

`getCurrentDream` filters `state.flags._dreamId` through `DREAMS.find(d => d.id === id)`, so even a tampered save where `_dreamId` contains `<script>...` resolves to `null` and the section is hidden — no path from state into the HTML.

`window.selectDream(dreamId)` writes `st.flags._dreamId = dreamId` without validation, but the value is then re-validated by `getCurrentDream` before any render uses it. The DREAMS lookup is the gate. The inline `onclick="selectDream('<d.id>')"` template uses only the static `d.id` literals ("restaurant", "apartment", "abroad", "investor", "celebrity") — none contain quote characters.

**Phase 2c — High-miss patterns checked:**
- *Sensitive-to-observability*: `addMessage` only receives static story strings concatenated with the static dream icon/title. No PII/secret leakage.
- *Allowlist semantic escape*: `getCurrentDream`'s `DREAMS.find` exact-match is the allowlist; tampered IDs return null cleanly.
- *Stale identity / control regression / fail-open*: Not applicable — single-player client-side game, no authorization decision in the new code.
- *Resource-bound*: `dream.milestones` is a fixed length-5 array; no attacker-influenced loop bounds.
- *Under-validated sink arg*: The pre-existing `renderActionCard` does `card.innerHTML = \`...${action.name}...${action.desc}...\``. This diff feeds it `dream.icon + " 梦想：" + dream.name` and `"进度 " + progress + "% · 当前里程碑：" + curTitle` — all components are static or numeric. The unsafe pattern is pre-existing; the new code does not extend its taint surface.

**Threat model**: This is a fully client-side browser game (state in localStorage, no server, no auth boundary). The "attacker = the user" for state mutation, and DREAMS is the trust boundary the renderer enforces. A malicious save file shared between users still cannot inject HTML because every renderer-visible string is sourced from `DREAMS.find()` rather than directly from state.

No security vulnerabilities introduced by this change.

No security findings.

Summary of analysis:
- **DOM sinks** (`dreamEl.innerHTML`, `showModal({body})` with inline `onclick="selectDream('...')"`, and the action card `card.innerHTML` consumer of the new action's `name`/`desc`) are fed exclusively from the statically-defined `DREAMS` array literal in `dreams.js` (hardcoded `icon`, `name`, `desc`, `title`, `story`, `id`) plus numeric `progress`. No state-derived or user-supplied string reaches these sinks unescaped.
- **`window.selectDream(dreamId)`** writes `st.flags._dreamId` without validating the argument, but every reader (`getCurrentDream`) re-validates via `DREAMS.find(d => d.id === id)`, so a tampered save / malicious caller resolves to `null` and the section silently hides — the allowlist gate holds.
- **`StateManager.addMessage`** receives only static dream strings (icon + title + story). No PII or secret reaches a logging/observability sink.
- **Daily pipeline integration** (`checkDreamProgress`) reads numeric state thresholds (cash, skill levels, fame, affinity counts) and has no authorization role; the only side effects are setting flags and emitting the static narrative message.
- No new shell/SQL/eval/fs/SSRF/deserialization/IaC/CI/auth-gate surface introduced.

The change is a pure narrative/UI feature with no security-relevant inputs from outside the trust boundary defined by `DREAMS`.
